assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new window on the universe: the detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies with a cubic-kilometre instrument in Antarctic ice, later followed by evidence for individual sources. As an experimentalist in astroparticle physics I value that this required a genuinely new detector concept and decades of instrument development, and that the result is unambiguous and important for cosmic-ray origin and multi-messenger astronomy.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit lists only Francis Halzen, who conceived and led IceCube and its AMANDA precursor. IceCube is a large collaboration, so a fair configuration may need to recognise other instrument pioneers, but the supplied credited names support only Halzen, so a sole-laureate configuration is proposed.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux first reported in 2013 and since confirmed with several independent event channels; source evidence (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) strengthens it. Mature enough for recognition, though source-level associations are still maturing.
uncertainties: A single-person credit may not reflect the collaborative nature of the discovery or the contributions of other detector pioneers not in the supplied names.
Independent confirmation from other neutrino telescopes such as KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD is still developing; my own knowledge of the detailed source evidence is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measurement of the last unknown neutrino mixing angle theta-13 through reactor antineutrino disappearance was an unexpectedly large value that made leptonic CP violation searches feasible. It is a clean, precise and decisive experimental measurement relying on carefully designed identical near and far detectors.
assessment.attribution: The supplied names cover the leaders of Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim), which gives a natural three-person configuration. Double Chooz and T2K contributed concurrent evidence, and the relative credit between the experiments and their founders is a sensitive matter.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple independent experiments and a decade of improved precision. The 2015 prize for neutrino oscillations leaves this as a clear follow-on, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Possible objection that the 2015 prize already covers neutrino oscillations.
Priority among Daya Bay, RENO and Double Chooz is contested, and how credit is split from collaboration leadership roles is not obvious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, using the magic wavelength to eliminate light shifts, reaches fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and has transformed time keeping, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea is original, simple in concept and experimentally decisive.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated it; Ye led the highest-accuracy realisations. Both names are in the supplied credit and form a defensible two-person prize. Earlier contributors to ion clocks and combs have been recognised in earlier prizes.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with independent confirmations at several national metrology institutes and comparisons across continents. A redefinition of the SI second is anticipated but not yet adopted.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes on frequency combs and ion control may be raised.
Whether other contributors such as Hall or Ludlow should share credit is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered the first precision full-sky CMB temperature and polarisation maps, fixing the cosmological parameters of the standard Lambda-CDM model at percent level and detecting reionisation. As a space-instrumentation experimentalist I regard the combination of instrument design and systematic control as exemplary.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument scientist and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. The supplied three names are a coherent configuration, but the WMAP science team was large and COBE and Planck overlap.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with independent confirmation by Planck and ground experiments. The question is whether the achievement is distinct enough from the 2006 and 2019 prizes.
uncertainties: Potential redundancy with the COBE prize of 2006 and the cosmology prize of 2019.
Planck superseded WMAP precision and the committee may prefer a broader CMB recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of kilonovae powered by r-process decay, and their discovery following GW170817, established neutron-star mergers as a site of heavy-element production. This ties together nuclear physics, gravitational waves and observational astronomy with a clear observational signature.
assessment.attribution: Metzger and Kasen made decisive theoretical and modelling contributions, and Tanvir led an early observational detection, including the GRB 130603B candidate. The original Li and Paczynski proposal is not among the supplied names, which weakens a clean credit allocation.
assessment.maturity: GW170817 gives one multi-messenger event with a well-studied kilonova, and further events have been ambiguous. Interpretation of the r-process yield remains debated.
uncertainties: Only one definitive event so far, so the strength of independent confirmation is limited.
Credit allocation between theory, early GRB candidates and GW170817 follow-up is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials. The originality and the breadth of subsequent work are substantial.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero led the 2018 experimental discoveries. This theory-plus-experiment pairing is a natural configuration, though Cao and Fatemi and other experimentalists contributed.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups across several moire platforms, yet the mechanism of superconductivity is still debated, so understanding is not fully settled.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is unresolved and the field is still evolving rapidly.
Early experimental contributors such as Yuan Cao and Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's students are not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Bose-Hubbard model and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, and now give programmable quantum simulators of many-body physics. The conceptual and experimental impact across condensed matter and quantum information is large.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied the theoretical proposal with Jaksch and colleagues, Greiner and Bloch performed the landmark Mott insulator experiments, and Dalibard and Cirac also contributed. Choosing three out of five is difficult and the choice reflects an interpretation of decisive contributions.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a tool and well replicated, though the scientific payoff for solving open many-body problems is still emerging.
uncertainties: Selection among five credited names is arbitrary to some degree.
The community may view quantum simulation as better recognised through a broader quantum technologies prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Laser wakefield acceleration promises accelerating gradients orders of magnitude above conventional radio-frequency cavities. The proposal and the 2004 monoenergetic electron beam experiments are original, and as an instrument builder I value the potential to change accelerator technology.
assessment.attribution: Tajima proposed the concept with John Dawson, who is deceased, and Leemans and Malka led the major experimental demonstrations, though the 2004 results involved several groups. The three-person credit is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Experimental proof is solid, but practical applications such as a collider or a compact free-electron laser are not yet realised, and the 2018 prize on chirped pulse amplification partly overlaps.
uncertainties: Practical impact is still prospective, so recognition could be premature.
Dawson and the 2004 experimental groups are not fully captured by the supplied names, and overlap with the 2018 prize is a concern.
